judgment.rationale: First SFI (Grade R, Term 2, Emergent Writing, Sub-strand 'Handwriting'): 'Develops large muscle control: works in pairs or on own to form letters with their bodies'. Second SFI (Grade R, Term 3, Emergent Writing, Sub-strand 'Emergent Handwriting:'): 'Develops fine motor skills for strengthening hand muscles: forms letters with play dough, threads lacing cards, beads'. These are two distinct printed bullets expressing complementary motor foundations for emergent letter formation: whole-body/gross-motor letter shaping and hand-muscle/fine-motor manipulation with dough, lacing cards and beads. They cohere substantively because both serve the same handwriting-readiness goal of forming letters within the same Grade R Emergent Writing skill area, which is more than generic repetition or shared wording. A developmental claim is not supported: each endpoint's own audit_context merge_reason enumerates the bullets in its term's table row, and both the Term 2 row and the Term 3 row independently include a 'fine motor skills' bullet and a 'large muscle control' bullet. Fine- and gross-motor work therefore run in parallel across Grade R terms, so proficiency in body-letter formation is not shown to enable hand-muscle strengthening; the Term 3 fine-motor bullet is the counterpart of the Term 2 fine-motor bullet, not a successor of the Term 2 gross-motor bullet. relatesTo is symmetric with null direction and retains canonical endpoint order. Limitations: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and all ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, including merged Grade R / Term banner nodes; the shared ancestor in the nomination is only the Grade R grouping, and token/tag overlap is low, so hierarchy and overlap signals were not treated as semantic evidence.

The direction is therefore earlier Term to later Term within the same grade, which is permitted. Recognising one's own name in print gives the concrete anchor of known printed material from which letter- and word-boundary discrimination is then taught, so proficiency in the Term 1 skill supports success in the Term 4 skill. LC tag/text overlap ('emergent writing', 'identifies', 'print') confirms shared print-awareness strand rather than merely coincidental wording. The evidence shows no substantive expansion in scope, independence, or complexity of one over the other, and identical Grade and Term give no developmental ordering, so a directional buildsTowards is not supported; the coherence is nonetheless substantive rather than generic word overlap (shared token 'writes' and LC tag 'emergent writing' alone would not suffice). Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all nodes carry upstream audit/merge context, which limits but does not contradict this reading.
